name: openreadout
description: Read raw lab-instrument files (microscopy, screening plates, electron microscopy, flow cytometry, electrophysiology, NMR, FT-IR/Raman, mass spectrometry, chromatography, plate readers, qPCR) without vendor software.
long_description: One static binary that reads lab-instrument files and returns what is in them: images, channels, pixel size, signals, spectra, plate reads and acquisition metadata; shows a preview image of the data; validates file integrity; answers the usual analysis question (chromatogram peaks, standard curves, Cq values, NMR peaks, spike features, gated counts, many-file tables joined to sample sheets); and exports to OME-TIFF, OME-Zarr, mzML, Parquet, NWB, JCAMP-DX, Allotrope ASM or RDML with read-back verification. Offline, no telemetry, never modifies the source file. Every tool is read-only except export, check with report=true, batch with output and index, which only write new files (exports are verified).

tools.name: openreadout_info
tools.description: What a file or data-set directory holds, from its headers: images, tables, traces, spectra, plate, experiment, assurance; view=full|structure|explain|format, or ask a question in words

tools.name: openreadout_check
tools.description: Integrity check with findings; against=FILE compares two files (e.g. a source and its export); report=true builds a privacy-reviewed diagnostic bundle

tools.name: openreadout_preview
tools.description: A picture of the data (image plane, composite, projection, zoomed region, trace, spectrum or plate heat map) as image content

tools.name: openreadout_stats
tools.description: Pixel statistics per channel and image: min, max, mean, std, percentiles, histogram, zero and saturated fractions; per=plane|well|field

tools.name: openreadout_trace
tools.description: One window of one sweep of a signal or 1-D spectrum in physical units: statistics, argmax_axis_value and samples

tools.name: openreadout_table
tools.description: Rows of a table (FCS events, plate reads, event, spike and peak tables); FCS optionally compensated, transformed and gated; filter and count

tools.name: openreadout_spectra
tools.description: Mass spectra of an MS run: scan headers filtered and counted, or one spectrum's m/z and intensity arrays (scan, index, or ms_level + nth)

tools.name: openreadout_analyze
tools.description: Analyses with documented methods: kind=peaks, chromatogram, nmr-peaks, ephys-features, spikes, qpcr, assay or gate

tools.name: openreadout_export
tools.description: Convert to OME-TIFF, OME-Zarr, Parquet, mzML, NWB, JCAMP-DX, Allotrope ASM or RDML with read-back verification, or write an embedded attachment

tools.name: openreadout_batch
tools.description: Any measure or analysis over many files as one tidy table, joined to sample sheets and summarized by group; measure=summarize regroups a saved table

tools.name: openreadout_link
tools.description: Group files that measured the same sample across instruments, with the evidence and a confidence

tools.name: openreadout_index
tools.description: Catalog every data set under directories into an index of Parquet tables (headers only; resumable)

tools.name: openreadout_search
tools.description: Search an index: data sets matching a query such as objective=63x channel~GFP acquired<2020

tools.name: openreadout_watch
tools.description: Watch directories where instruments write: new data sets, planes and scans, completion, stalls and live QC events since a cursor

prompts.name: summarize_file
prompts.text: Summarize the lab-instrument file ${arguments.file}: call openreadout_info (view=explain for an account in words), look at it with openreadout_preview, then report what it is, what was measured and how, when, and anything unusual. Only state values the tools returned.

prompts.name: check_file
prompts.description: Check a file and explain problems
prompts.text: Check whether ${arguments.file} is intact with openreadout_check. Explain every finding in plain language (cause, affected data) and suggest how to salvage what is readable.

prompts.name: convert_to_open_format
prompts.text: Convert ${arguments.file} to the open format that fits its data (OME-TIFF or OME-Zarr for images, mzML for mass spectra, Allotrope ASM for plate reads; CSV via the CLI for tables and traces) with openreadout_export, after checking its size with openreadout_info. Report the output path and whether it was verified.
